name: security-audit-log-reader-authority-review
intent: Audit query scope across partition expansion, cursor and export publication
artifacts: Event schema, log-reader roles, tenant/project filters, retention and export endpoints.
trace: Follow a caller query into effective log scope and serializer fields. Differentiate read access to security events from permission to read credentials/PII inside them.
experiment: Query synthetic audit events through a scoped reader capability, then alter the continuation/export query or partition while preserving the same visible filter. Inspect final event fields and artifact audience against the immutable scope.
disproof: An audit-event count or event type may be intentionally visible; require an actual field/object policy violation.
repair: Constrain reader scope and redact unnecessary sensitive fields, preserving authorized incident response and audit fidelity.
branch_decisions: Evaluate reader scope, query filters, export jobs and fields independently from permission to perform the logged actions. Audit readers may intentionally see security-relevant cross-user metadata; establish which contents remain protected. A redacted UI does not prove raw export/search restrictions, and a permitted event count is not automatically a complete log disclosure.
operational_method: Specialize in audit query/export scope carried across the UI, query DSL, cursor and async result link. Retain the immutable tenant/project scope attached to the reader capability and compare it with index/partition selection and field projection after query rewriting. Test a scoped synthetic search, a forged continuation/export context and the final redacted event payload. Ordinary one-object API access without audit query fan-out belongs in generic object/property review.
